full_judgment:
3. The short fact of the case is that the plaintiffs-petitioners brought the Title Suit No. 180 of 1990 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 on 3-6-1990 in favour of the respondent-opposite party in respect of 14 decimals of land under suit Plot No. 1057 of SA Khatian No. 90 of Mouza Teordah No. 254 was collusive, inoperative, illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff-petitioners who claimed themselves to be necessary parties was not in pleading in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988. Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 was brought by defendant-opposite party for declaration of his title in 14 decimals of said land. The said suit was transferred to the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah for trial and the Title Suit No. 180 of 1990 was renumbered as 60 of 1994. 

 4. The plaintiff-petitioners case, in brief, is that 25 decimals of land under SA Khatian No. 90, Mouza Teordah No. 254 was taken on lease by one Mubarak Mridha from CS recorded tenant Ratikanta and others. While he was possessing thereof he sold the same to Abdur Rashid Miah by a registered kabala dated 2-3-1965. While Abdur Rashid was in possession thereof by mutating his name and by payment of rent thereof he sold the same to the plaintiff petitioner Nos. 13 by three separate kabalas dated 12-11-86. The plaintiff-petitioner No. 4, the father of plaintiff-petitioner, possessed the suit land on their behalf along with other lands of the suit plot by paying rent and, by mutating their name and amalgamating the same with his other adjoining nonsuited lands under his own Plot Nos. 1058 and 1059 by establishing a paddy crushing mill and Chatal thereon. On 8-7-91 respondent-opposite party secretly managed to obtain the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 and thereafter threatened to dispossess the plaintiff-petitioners from the 14 decimals of said land by virtue of the said ex parte decree dated 3690. So the plaintiff-petitioners brought the Title Suit No. 180 of 1990 and thereafter the said suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 which was filed for declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 is not binding on them. The suit was dismissed by his judgment and decree dated 21-11-1991. The plaintiff-petitioners filed the Title Appeal No. 216 of 1991 against the dismissal order. The appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenidah who was pleased to allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and by the said judgment the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 was sent on remand to the Trial Court for fresh trial analogously with Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 (a suit brought by respondent-petitioner Lutfur Rahman for declaration of his title in 14 decimals of land and for partition by metes and bounds) by taking into consideration the evidence, documents already filed by either party and by giving an opportunity to the parties to adduce further oral evidence, if necessary. Accordingly, the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 was analogously tried with Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 brought by the plaintiff-petitioners for their declaration of title in 14 decimals of land, all these three suits between the same parties over the same suit land.
